title: SLO-driven deployment governor with dynamic rollback bands
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a deployment governor that automatically triggers safe, graded rollback actions for canary / A/B / shadow traffic based on fused SLO signals (latency P50/P95, request error rate, token cost drift, throughput degradation). The governor should use dynamic, traffic-aware thresholds ("bands") rather than fixed cutoffs to reduce false positives, and expose tuning knobs to SREs and platform owners. It must be conservative by default (fail-open = keep serving unless strong evidence) and allow configurable aggressiveness for high-risk customers.
acceptance_criteria: The governor evaluates at least four signals (p50 latency, p95 latency, error rate, token-cost per request) and produces a single risk score per canary cohort every 10s
Automatic actions supported: reduce canary weight by 50%, route to fallback model variant, or fully abort the rollout. Actions must be reversible and logged in rollout history
False-positive rate on historical traffic simulation < 2% for 6-month production traces when using default band configuration
Platform dashboard shows per-cohort z-score, risk score, and the reason(s) for any automatic action
Playbook for manual override and emergency rollback documented and linked from Console
design_notes: Signal fusion: compute normalized deltas (z-scores) against an adaptive baseline per-customer and per-model; aggregate via a weighted sum where weights are tunable per project

Dynamic bands: define green/amber/red bands as percentiles of the baseline distribution (e.g., amber = 95th percentile drift window) instead of fixed thresholds; bands auto-adjust over a sliding 30m window to tolerate diurnal changes
Adaptive threshold tuning: use EWMA + recent quantile tracking for latency and token cost; for error rate use Bayesian interval estimate to avoid noisy proportions at low traffic

Decision rule: require a combination of (a) risk score above red, or (b) two independent signals in amber + one in red, or (c) sustained amber for configurable duration (default 120s) before triggering partial weight reduction
Stability: include hysteresis to avoid flapping (min action interval, backoff on repeated oscillations), and require stabilization period after any automatic action before allowing another escalation
Cohort awareness: compute signals per canary cohort and per-cohort baseline; global cohort aggregation is used only for low-traffic cohorts to increase statistical power
Token-cost drift: compare realized token cost per request to expected cost profile for the prompt/template cohort; treat sustained >10% increase as higher weight in risk score
Graceful actions: default partial rollback is to cut canary traffic to 10% of prior weight and shift remaining to the last known-good model variant (or fallback), with notification to owners
Privacy & data retention: only aggregated metrics used for decisioning; raw prompts are never sent into the governor service; align with existing KMS/audit workflows
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (sim + dry-run): run the governor against 6 months of historical traces in the sim harness; measure false-positive/negative rates and tune band parameters (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (observability-only): deploy governor in read-only mode in staging + canary region (no automated actions, only suggestions and risk scores surfaced in Console) (1 week)
Phase 2 (opt-in automated): enable automated partial rollback for non-critical tenants with additional guardrails (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (default conservative): flip automated mode on by default for new canaries with conservative bands and telemetry (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (tune & expand): iterate on thresholds and per-customer weights, onboard Dedicated customers with opt-out option
test_plan: Unit tests for each signal normalization and aggregation step
Integration tests for action execution path (partial weight reduction, full abort, route to fallback)
Chaos tests: induce high-latency, token-cost spike, and error bursts independently and in combinations to validate decision rules
Regression simulation against 6 months of historical production traces to verify FP < 2% and FN < 5% for severe incidents
E2E: canary that intentionally degrades in staging to validate console messaging, notifications, and rollback behavior
